My goal is to be matched with my most preferred school from the set of schools that would accept me. The "obtainable set" is determined by the school priorities, not my ranking. My ranking only determines which school I get *if* multiple schools would accept me.

*   **School z:** I have priority 2 at z.
*   **School x:** I have priority 2 at x.
*   **School w:** I have priority 1 at w.
*   **School y:** I have priority 1 at y.

Since I have top priority at w and y, they will definitely be in my obtainable set. I prefer w > y, so I want to rank w higher than y. Since I also have priority 2 at x and z, whether or not these schools are in my obtainable set depends on the other applicants. Since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, it is likely that x and z will be competitive.

My preference order is z > x > w > y.

I want to maximize my chances of getting z or x if possible. Since w and y are guaranteed to be in my obtainable set, and I prefer w to y, I want to rank w higher than y.

Therefore, I should rank my preferences in their true order, since this will maximize my utility given the obtainable set.

Next, I should rank x second.

Therefore, my ranking should be z > x > y > w.
